title: Throughput Provenance Sentinel: cross-model TPS & p95 regression harness
creator: Diego Morales
description: Build a sustainable, model-agnostic microbenchmark harness ("The Provenance Sentinel") that produces stable tokens-per-second (TPS) fingerprints and p95 latency provenance for core models. This ticket covers design, implementation, CI integration, dashboards, and alerting for automated regression detection when model or infra changes affect serving economics. The harness must be reproducible, parameterizable (seq length, batch size, concurrency, kv-warm/kv-cold), and lightweight enough to run nightly and on PRs for runtime/kernel changes.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can profile at least 5 core models (autoregressive and chat variants) with consistent config across runs
Recorded metrics include: tokens/sec, p95/p99 generation latency, per-token CPU/GPU utilization, batch-efficiency, and KV-warmup delta
Nightly CI job publishes time-series to runtime-performance dashboard and archives raw traces to S3 for forensic analysis
Regression detector flags p95 increase >10% or tokens/sec drop >8% with configurable sensitivity and creates a Linear incident ticket
Canary PR runs (fast mode) execute a lightweight subset and block merges on high-confidence regressions
Documentation and runbook published in internal Confluence and linked in the dashboard
implementation_steps: Prototype microbench CLI that accepts model id, prompt profile, seq length distribution, target concurrency, and batching policy
Instrument harness to emit structured telemetry (OpenTelemetry spans + Prometheus counters) and attach context tags (model_version, kernel_profile, quantization)
Create workload presets: short-chat (8-16 tokens output), long-form (512 tokens), mixed-burst (50/5/200 split)
Integrate with nightly CI (GitHub Actions) and a fast PR runner (subset of presets) with resource isolation
Implement regression detector using median-of-rolling-window baseline with Mann-Whitney U test for non-parametric significance and configurable thresholds
Build Grafana dashboard panels: TPS fingerprint, p95 heatmap by preset/model, batch utilization, recent regression alerts
Add automatic artifact links: failing PR, raw trace S3 path, kernel-selection diff, and CPU/GPU flamegraphs
Document runbook: how to triage, rerun experiments, and bisect infra vs model causes
notes_and_decisions: Decision: use non-parametric test (Mann-Whitney U) because latency distributions are often non-normal and contain heavy tails
Decision: preserve a rolling 28-day baseline for each model+preset combination; baseline window configurable per project
Trade-off: nightly full-run is slower but provides richer signals; PR-run is a sampled subset to keep feedback fast
Implementation note: prefer in-process lightweight harness to reduce orchestration complexity; use a containerized job for CI reproducibility
Risk: noisy multi-tenant GPU hosts can inflate variance — mitigations: pinned nodes for nightly, statistical smoothing, and warm-up policies
